paragraphs: Mentioned in Megillah 10a, where he introduces his exposition of the Megillah with a text from this passage. Tosafot explains that the reading is Ofran, not Efron.
There, 15a: Rabbah bar Ofran said in the name of Rabbi Elazar, etc.[^1][^2]

notes.text: פתח פיתחא is the idiom for opening a homiletic exposition, not opening a physical door for someone. The source’s כשדרס is read contextually as “when he expounded,” without changing its letters.

The checked Megillah passages contain the Ofran exposition and Ofran reporting Elazar at 10b and 15b in the consulted digital arrangement. Tosafot there distinguishes Ofran from Efron. Hyman’s supplied 10a and 15a locators remain visible, without a Hebrew locator or name repair.
